subject: Embeddings endpoint latency increase after catalog variant swap — urgent
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena@datasyn.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: ops@datasyn.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden latency increases on /v1/embeddings (post-catalog change)

Hi Dylan —

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95 and p99 for your embeddings endpoint around 2026-12-20 08:45 UTC after the catalog swap your team ran. Latency for our bulk indexing jobs increased from ~120ms p95 to ~1.2s and p99s spiked to 2.5–3s. We attached a short sample trace and a timeline. This is causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline and blocking a release.

Can you confirm whether any model variant swaps or routing changes were deployed in the us-west region around that time? We need an ETA for mitigation or rollback — this is impacting our customers.

Thanks,
Elena
Ops Lead, Datasyn

Attachments: latency_sample_120s.txt (text), timeline.csv (referenced)
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Elena Mendez <elena@datasyn.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-20T09:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency increases on /v1/embeddings (post-catalog change)

Elena — thank you for the report and the traces. I'm escalating immediately. Short summary: we performed a catalog variant swap at ~08:30 UTC that promoted a new quantized variant for the catalog embedding model in us-west-2; intended to reduce cost. We're rolling up engineering now to validate whether the promoted variant has an execution path causing long tail latency.

Immediate next steps (internal):
- Looping in Engineering (Neha) and Customer Success (Marissa) to triage and update you within 1 hour.
- If we cannot identify a quick mitigation, we'll roll back the variant to the prior stable variant and pin the catalog.

Elena — I will send an ETA in the hour and request permission to rollback if needed.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-20T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency increases on /v1/embeddings (post-catalog change)

Team — digging in. Early observations:
- Catalog change: variant 'embed-quant-v3' was promoted in us-west-2 at 2026-12-20T08:28:47Z (see catalog-change-log.pdf attached).
- Telemetry shows an uptick in KV cache miss rate for the promoted variant and a bimodal tokenization path triggered for a subset of requests.
- p95 jumped from ~110ms to ~1.1s; p99 now hitting 2.6–3.1s. Error rates unchanged (no 5xx spike), so CPU/GPU OOMs unlikely.

Hypothesis: the quantization path introduced a slower fallback for certain sequence-lengths when the tokenization aligns poorly with shard boundaries, producing long-tail inference times. I have asked inference team to capture nvprof traces and the runtime will capture a microprofile.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Roll back to 'embed-quant-v2' (previous variant) — fastest to restore SLOs.
2) Apply a temporary routing rule: route requests with sequence length > 512 to the stable variant (adds complexity).
3) Disable the new variant globally and re-run offline perf tests.

I'll take ownership of the rollback if we approve. Please advise on customer communication cadence.

—Neha
Sr. SW Eng, Inference Optimization

Attachments: catalog-change-log.pdf
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Mendez <elena@datasyn.ai>, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-20T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency increases on /v1/embeddings (post-catalog change)

Elena — I'm on this with Dylan and Neha. Two quick asks while we triage:
- Can you share the ingestion job window (UTC) and an example document that triggers the slow path? That will help us reproduce quickly.
- If we proceed with a rollback we'll target a maintenance window now; is immediate rollback acceptable to Datasyn?

Planned customer comms (if rollback approved): short email saying we identified a correlation with a catalog variant promotion, we plan a rollback to previous stable variant, expected impact minimal and we will confirm when complete.

—Marissa
Customer Success Manager
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Elena Mendez <elena@datasyn.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-20T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Update: rolling back catalog variant for Datasyn now

Elena — per Neha's analysis and with your permission, we're rolling back the catalog promotion for the embedding model in us-west-2 to the prior stable variant ('embed-quant-v2'). Expected timeline: rollback will be initiated immediately and should complete within ~8 minutes; we will monitor p95/p99 and confirm once back to baseline.

If we see any degradation during rollback we will pause and open a private channel. We'll follow up with a short post-mortem and a plan to harden validation gating for future catalog promotions.

Thanks for flagging this promptly — we know this blocks Datasyn's release.

—Dylan

Attachment: datasyn_request-form.docx (signed rollback approval attached by customer)
From: Elena Mendez <elena@datasyn.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@datasyn.ai
Date: 2026-12-21T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Update: rolling back catalog variant for Datasyn now

Thanks Dylan & team — rollback worked. Our p95/p99 are back within acceptable bounds (p95 ~130ms, p99 ~240ms) and ingestion resumed. Appreciate the quick turnaround and the offer of a post-mortem. Two asks for the post-mortem:
- Please include exact root cause (runtime path + data shapes) and a plan to add pre-promotion smoke tests that mimic our bulk ingest shapes.
- We need a change-control checkbox for any future catalog variant promotions that could affect long-tail latency.

Elena
Ops Lead, Datasyn
